svg.aria-label: Flowchart of the three ways java.lang.Integer.IntegerCache gets filled in JDK 21.0.7. The top half quotes the real static initialiser verbatim beside three note panels. The bottom half is one straight-line clinit flowchart with two decision points, not three independent branches. It begins at IntegerCache clinit, sets int h to 127 by default, then decision one asks whether VM.getSavedProperty of java.lang.Integer.IntegerCache.high is non-null; if yes a side box clamps h with Math.max of the parsed property and 127 then Math.min against Integer.MAX_VALUE minus 128 minus 1, which means the property can only raise high and never lower it, measured with AutoBoxCacheMax equal to 50 leaving the boundary at 127. Both branches rejoin at high equals h, where low equals minus 128 is marked static final and fixed by JLS section 5.1.7. On the trunk, unconditionally and on every path, CDS.initializeFromArchive of IntegerCache.class runs and either writes archivedCache from the CDS archive or leaves it null. Then size is computed as high minus low plus one, and decision two tests archivedCache being null or size exceeding archivedCache length. A single vertical stub fans out on a shared horizontal bus to three outcome panels: outcome a, the true branch with default high, constructing 256 new Integer objects; outcome b, the true branch after the property raised high to 1000, where the archived subgraph still initialises but size 1129 exceeds the archived length of 256 so 1129 objects are constructed anyway; and outcome c, the false branch, where the archived array is mapped with nothing constructed and zero allocation. All three outcome panels repeat that low equals minus 128 is fixed by JLS section 5.1.7.
svg.text: Three ways IntegerCache gets filled — one <clinit>, two decisions, three outcomes
SECTION 1 — THE REAL STATIC INITIALISER, JDK 21.0.7 lib/src.zip

svg.text: HOW THE CONTROL FLOW ACTUALLY RUNS

g.text: One straight-line <clinit> with TWO decision points — not three
independent branches. It yields THREE outcomes.
1. high: default 127. Math.max(parseInt(prop), 127) means the saved
property can only RAISE high, never lower it. Measured with
== valueOf(127) true, 128 false — unchanged from default.
2. CDS.initializeFromArchive is called UNCONDITIONALLY, after high
is fixed — it sits on the trunk, never on a branch.
3. The size test then picks: map the archived array (nothing built)
or construct size new Integer objects in a loop.
low = −128 is static final with a literal initialiser, fixed by JLS §5.1.7.
[0.008s][info][cds,heap] Patching native pointers in heap region
With -Xshare:off NO cds,heap lines are printed at all — the archive is
not consulted and the array is constructed. No Boolean cache subgraph
exists: Boolean has no cache class, only static final TRUE / FALSE.

svg.text: MEASURED — RAISING high, AND WHY IT IS NOT A SYSTEM PROPERTY

g.text: java.lang.Integer$IntegerCache STILL fires, but size = 1129 is greater
than archivedCache.length = 256, so the array is rebuilt anyway.
-XX:AutoBoxCacheMax=1000 does NOT make the value visible to
returned null. It is a SAVED VM property, readable only through
Domain: retry counts and DEPOSIT_LIMITED counts on an Application.

svg.text: DECISION 1 — is the saved property present?
low = −128 — static final, fixed by JLS §5.1.7
UNCONDITIONAL — on every path, after high is fixed
writes archivedCache if a CDS archive holds the subgraph;
leaves archivedCache null otherwise. This is the trunk.
int size = (high - low) + 1; // 256 at default high
